subject: Exit timing, notice offsets & termination-for-convenience alternatives
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <legal@acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@acme.com, Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — notice window & termination language

Rachel — attaching our consolidated redline for the MSA and the Order Form. High level: Acme is requesting clearer opt-out timing and stronger unilateral termination-for-convenience protections because we’re planning a phased migration across multiple business units. Key asks: 1) a 45-day notice window prior to auto-renewal, 2) ability for Acme to terminate for convenience with 90 days’ notice, and 3) a requirement that Redwood provide transition assistance (knowledge transfer + data export) for up to 60 days after termination.

We left comments in the PDF on sections 2.1, 3.4, and 12.2. Please confirm your legal’s position on the 90-day convenience termination and the scope of transition assistance (we expect playbooks and access to KV caches for export).

Attachments: ACME_Redline_MSA.pdf (PDF), Order_Form_ACME_redline.docx (DOCX)

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Smith
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp
legal@acme.com

---
On prior discussions: we flagged termination mechanics in procurement call last week; hope we can resolve without a long redline cycle.

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <legal@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — notice window & termination language

Jordan — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. We want to keep this practical so the deal can go ahead without leaving migration risk open. Initial thoughts:

- Auto-renew/opt-out: Redwood is generally comfortable with a 45-day opt-out window prior to renewal, provided that the Order Form calls out the anniversary date explicitly and that opt-out is per-Order Form (so different pilots don’t automatically cancel enterprise capacity).

- Termination for convenience: Redwood prefers mutual termination-for-convenience (either party) with notice rather than an Acme-only unilateral right. That said, we can propose a hybrid: mutual 60-day termination for convenience during the initial term, moving to 90 days after the first renewal. That gives both sides runway and reduces churn risk.

- Transition assistance: agree to provide transition support; propose we define a scoped "migration assistance" SOW (capped hours + objectives) rather than an open-ended 60-day obligation. We’re open to 60 days of cooperation for production handoffs, but with defined deliverables and a not-to-exceed bandwidth commitment.

I'll loop in Laura (legal) to put suggested redlines in-line so we can return a clean PDF. Can we schedule a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow to get to yes?

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_v3_proposal_redline.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com

P.S. Karthis (cc) will handle contracting logistics once legal flags are aligned.

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Smith <legal@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — notice window & termination language

Jordan / team — I reviewed Acme's redline and Rachel's proposal. Below are concise suggested positions Redwood legal will push for; I’ve included redlineable snippets you can paste into the document. Our objective: close language that limits operational exposure and keeps the commercial relationship intact.

1) Auto‑renew and opt‑out
- Position: 12‑month renewal term. Either party may elect not to renew by providing written notice at least forty‑five (45) days prior to the end of the then‑current Term. Notice shall be effective on the date received.

2) Termination for Convenience
- Position: Mutual termination for convenience by either party on prior written notice. During the initial term, notice shall be sixty (60) days; after the first Renewal Term, notice shall be ninety (90) days.
- Suggested redline: "Either party may terminate this Agreement, without cause, by providing the other party with written notice equal to the notice period applicable to the then‑current term (60 days during the Initial Term; 90 days following the first Renewal Term)."

3) Transition and wind‑down
- Position: Redwood will provide "Migration Assistance" as set forth in an attachment SOW limited to X hours or Y deliverables, to be agreed upon. Redwood is not responsible for redesigning customer architectures during wind‑down but will provide access to exported artifacts and reasonable personnel time to support cutover activities for up to sixty (60) calendar days post‑termination. Billing continues until transfer completion or the end of the notice period, whichever is later.

4) Early termination economics
- Position: If termination occurs for convenience prior to Minimum Commitment fulfillment, Redwood may invoice for (i) unpaid fees for services already delivered and (ii) a termination administration fee equal to the lesser of (A) three (3) months’ average recurring fees or (B) 25% of remaining committed fees, to compensate for capacity allocation and de‑provisioning costs.

Next steps we recommend: Karthik — please confirm whether Acme’s commercial team will accept a capped termination administration fee vs. a full TCV charge. Rachel — propose the call tomorrow 10:00 PT to walk Acme through these points; Jordan, please confirm availability. If you prefer, I can redline the attached PDF directly and return by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

[Attachment note: Suggested redline snippets included above; full PDF redline available on request.]

From: Jordan Smith <legal@acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@acme.com, Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form — notice window & termination language

Rachel / Laura — thanks for the quick review and for laying out Redwood's proposed compromise. Acme's position: we can accept mutual termination for convenience but would like the following clarifications in the redline before we sign off:

1) Notice timing: we are open to 60 days during the initial term and 90 days after first renewal, provided that the counting of the opt‑out notice for auto‑renewals is measured from the contract anniversary and that any notice window cannot be shortened by unilateral amendment.

2) Transition assistance: we accept a scoped SOW approach; however, Acme requires guaranteed access to exported data and a named technical contact during the 60‑day wind‑down. Please identify a point person and commit to response SLAs (72 hours for technical requests during wind‑down).

3) Early termination fee: Acme cannot accept a flat charge equal to a large percentage of remaining TCV. We will accept a capped fee equal to three (3) months’ average recurring fees (monthly MRC x 3) as a compromise.

If Redwood can reflect the three items above in a redline, Acme can proceed to sign and we can move to DocuSign. We are available for a 30‑minute call Thursday 9:30 PT to finalize language.

Regards,
Jordan Smith
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp
legal@acme.com

[Forwarded attachment: ACME_Redline_MSA.pdf (redline with inline comments)]
